title: Lecture 11 · Beta oxidation and lipid metabolism

blocks.html:
What to know

  • Fatty acids are activated to acyl-CoA. The carnitine shuttle moves long-chain acyl-CoA into the mitochondrial matrix for oxidation.
  • Beta oxidation removes two carbons at a time. Each cycle produces one acetyl-CoA, one NADH, and one FADH₂; the acetyl-CoA enters the TCA cycle.
  • Ketone bodies are made in the liver. When acetyl-CoA exceeds the cycle capacity, the liver makes acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate for other tissues, including the brain.
  • Fatty acid synthesis is not beta oxidation reversed. It uses acetyl-CoA carboxylase, malonyl-CoA, and NADPH, and it occurs in the cytoplasm.
  • Hormones switch storage and release. Insulin favors fat storage and lipoprotein lipase; glucagon and adrenaline favor lipolysis and beta oxidation.

Check

check.question: What does one cycle of beta oxidation produce?

options.text: One acetyl-CoA, one NADH, and one FADH₂

check.explanation: Each cycle shortens the fatty acid by two carbons and produces one acetyl-CoA plus one NADH and one FADH₂.
